'''Severn Cullis-Suzuki''' (born 30 November 1979{{Cn|date=March 2024}}) is a Canadian [[environmentalism|environmental activist]] and writer. She has spoken around the world about environmental issues, urging listeners to define their values, act with the future in mind and take individual responsibility. She is the daughter of Canadian environmentalist [[David Suzuki]].

== Biography ==
Severn Cullis-Suzuki was born and raised in [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]].<ref name="R1"/> Her mother is writer Tara Cullis. Her father, [[geneticist]] and environmental activist [[David Suzuki]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fernandes |first=Cesil |date=May 29, 2012 |title='Rio girl' Severn Cullis-Suzuki 20 years on |url=https://www.dw.com/en/rio-girl-severn-cullis-suzuki-20-years-on/a-15974444 |access-date=2021-09-11 |website=dw.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> is a third-generation [[Japanese Canadians|Japanese Canadian]].<ref name="R2"/> While attending [[Lord Tennyson Elementary School]] in [[French immersion|French Immersion]], at age 9, she founded the Environmental Children's Organization (ECO), a group of children dedicated to learning and teaching other youngsters about environmental issues.<ref name="speakers" /> In 1992, at age 12, Cullis-Suzuki raised money with members of ECO to attend the [[Earth Summit (1992)|Earth Summit]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. Along with group members Michelle Quigg, Vanessa Suttie, and Morgan Geisler, Cullis-Suzuki presented environmental issues from a youth perspective at the summit, where she was applauded for a speech to the delegates.<ref name="R3"/><ref name="R4"/> The video has since become a [[viral video|viral]] hit, popularly known as "The Girl Who Silenced the World for 5 Minutes".<ref name="R5"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.news.com.au/technology/environment/climate-change/nearly-30-years-before-greta-thunberg-a-12yearold-girl-shamed-world-leaders-at-the-united-nations/news-story/8e99d7fce5e0abae106ce73baa5209b7 |title=Nearly 30 years before Greta Thunberg, a 12-year-old girl shamed world leaders at the United Nations |work=[[news.com.au]]}}</ref>

In 1993, she was honoured in the [[United Nations Environment Programme]]'s [[Global 500 Roll of Honour]].<ref name="R6"/> In 1993, [[Doubleday (publisher)|Doubleday]] published her book ''Tell the World'', a 32-page book of environmental steps for families.

Cullis-Suzuki graduated from [[Yale University]] in 2002 with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in [[ecology]] and [[evolutionary biology]].<ref name="speakers"/> After Yale, Cullis-Suzuki spent two years travelling. Cullis-Suzuki co-hosted ''Suzuki's Nature Quest'', a children's television series that aired on [[Discovery Kids]] in 2002.

In early 2002, she helped launch an Internet-based [[think tank]] called The Skyfish Project.<ref name="theautobiography"/><ref name="R2"/> As a member of [[Kofi Annan]]'s Special Advisory Panel, she and members of the Skyfish Project brought their first project, a pledge called the "Recognition of Responsibility", to the [[Earth Summit 2002|World Summit on Sustainable Development]] in [[Johannesburg]] in August 2002.<ref name="speakers"/> The Skyfish Project disbanded in 2004 as Cullis-Suzuki turned her focus back to school. She enrolled in a graduate program at the [[University of Victoria]] to study [[ethnobotany]] under [[Nancy Turner]], finishing in 2007.<ref name="theautobiography"/>

Cullis-Suzuki is the main character in the documentary film ''Severn, the Voice of Our Children'', directed by Jean-Paul Jaud and released theatrically in France on November 10, 2010.

Cullis-Suzuki is an [[Earth Charter]] International Council Member.

==Personal life==
Married in 2008, Cullis-Suzuki lived with her husband and two sons in [[Haida Gwaii]], British Columbia, until August 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Hampson|first=Sarah|date=2007-07-09|title=Born green|language=en-CA|work=The Globe and Mail|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/life/relationships/born-green/article724099/|access-date=2021-10-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=A Fine Balance|url=https://www.earthisland.org/journal/index.php/magazine/entry/a_fine_balance/|access-date=2021-10-29|website=Earth Island Journal}}</ref> She moved to Vancouver, BC in order to start her new role as the Executive Director of the David Suzuki Foundation, which she began in September 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-07-11|title=bio|url=https://severncullissuzuki.com/bio/|access-date=2021-10-29|website=Severn Cullis-Suzuki|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-09|title=Severn Cullis-Suzuki to become executive director of David Suzuki Foundation|url=https://www.straight.com/news/severn-cullis-suzuki-to-become-executive-director-of-david-suzuki-foundation|access-date=2021-10-29|website=The Georgia Straight|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Quarantine as Ceremony: COVID-19 as an Opportunity to Quietly Rebel against the Dominant Langscape|url=https://terralingua.org/langscape_articles/quarantine-as-ceremony-covid-19-as-an-opportunity-to-quietly-rebel-against-the-dominant-langscape/|access-date=2021-10-29|website=Terralingua|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tretkoff|first=Ernie|date=2010|title=Christine McEntee Takes Office as AGU Executive Director|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1029/2010eo360005|journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union|volume=91|issue=36|pages=313|doi=10.1029/2010eo360005|bibcode=2010EOSTr..91..313T |issn=0096-3941|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

She is related to two [[NHL]] players, [[Nick Suzuki]] and [[Ryan Suzuki]].

== Cultural tributes ==
In 2009, French guitarist MattRach and his band used extracts from her 1992 speech in their track ''Human Bullshit''.<br>
In 2010, French DJ [[Laurent Wolf]] used her 1992 speech to turn it into a track : ''2012 - Not The End Of The World''.<br>
In 2016, NINSKEEN used part of her speech in the title ''Make Your Actions Reflect Your Words''.<br>
In 2017, the French group [[:fr:Grands Boulevards (groupe)|Grands Boulevards]] used an excerpt from her speech in the track ''Children of Light 8''.<br>
In 2017, the French group Way For Nothing used her speech in the title ''Consciousness''.<br>
In 2016 and 2018, the French musician Owen Le Guen used excerpts from her speech in the tracks ''Before Our Eyes'' and ''They Exist''.<br>
In 2018, a few lines of her speech can be heard from the vertical version of [[Alan Walker]]'s Different World music video.<br>
In 2018, [[:fr:Louise Tilleke|Louise Tilleke]] painted a portrait of Severn Cullis-Suzuki which she presented in her Parisian exhibition entitled Ask not the Earth….<br>
In 2020, more than 20 animation directors, under the artistic supervision of Simone Giampaolo, transposed her speech into a short film named ''Only a Child'', which they describe as "a visual poem". It won the [[The Ray Harryhausen Awards|Ray Harryhausen Award]] for best animated short film.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt16711504/|title=Only a Child (Short 2020)|website=www.imdb.com|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref><br>
In 2022, for the thirtieth anniversary, the artist Selfish Patterns uses parts of the speech in the track ''[https://soundcloud.com/selfish-patterns/1992a 1992]''.
